wiki_text: As of May 2026, NLNG Train 7 had reached approximately 92% completion (up from ~88% in February 2026) and was advancing into systems completion and pre-commissioning, with commissioning targeted within 2026 (some reports cite mid-2026). The $5 billion expansion is being executed by the SCD JV consortium (Saipem, Chiyoda, Daewoo), with FID taken in December 2019 and the EPC awarded in May 2020. Train 7, together with a Trains 1-6 debottlenecking project, will lift NLNG's nameplate capacity from ~22 mtpa to ~30 mtpa.

In September 2024 (at Gastech), NNPC Ltd stated it was in talks with investors to revive the long-stalled Brass LNG (~$20 billion, Bayelsa State) and Olokola/OK LNG (~$9.8 billion, Ogun State) projects, citing fiscal incentives under the Petroleum Industry Act 2021. As of mid-2026 these remained expressions of intent with no final investment decision, EPC award, or construction step; GEM continues to classify Brass LNG as shelved.

Golar LNG and NNPC signed a Project Development Agreement for a Nigeria FLNG deployment in June 2024 and initially targeted a 2024 FID, but Golar's CEO indicated FID was unlikely within 2024. By the third quarter of 2025, Golar had committed its only available newbuild FLNG capacity — the Mark II vessel (a conversion of the Moss-type carrier Fuji LNG, ~3.5 mtpa, delivery expected Q4 2027) — to a 20-year contract with Argentina's Southern Energy S.A., not Nigeria. No final investment decision on a Nigerian deployment had been reached, leaving the Nigeria project's vessel path uncertain.

topic: Wison FEED contract and project scope (2024)
wiki_text: In January 2024, China's Wison New Energies was reported to be contracted for two separate ~3 mtpa FLNG vessels offshore Nigeria — one for Transoceanic Gas & Power and one for Ace Gas & FLNG Company Ltd. On 6 December 2024, Wison New Energies signed a FEED contract with Ace Gas & FLNG for a 3 mtpa FLNG plus 230 MW power-barge project in the Escravos/Forcados hub region, to be moored ~10 km offshore and to process up to ~500 MMcf/d of gas (also yielding LPG, condensate and propane). The Ace Gas and Transoceanic projects are separate developments; no corporate parent linking Ace Gas to Transoceanic was found.
